Approximate quantiles added to the [approximate statistics](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/ncruces/go-sqlite3/ext/approx) package in #443.
The `database/sql` driver now uses `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions by default. You can change the default with `_txlock` (as previously), and as the docs state:
- [`LevelLinearizable`](https://pkg.go.dev/database/sql#IsolationLevel) transactions are always `EXCLUSIVE`;
- [`LevelSerializable`](https://pkg.go.dev/database/sql#IsolationLevel) transactions are always `IMMEDIAT

Removed [`FCNTL_NULL_IO`](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/c_fcntl_begin_atomic_write.html#sqlitefcntlnullio), which was broken and impossible to use correctly.
Used to implement bitwise aggregates `bit_and` and `bit_or`, and a new [approximate statistics](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/ncruces/go-sqlite3/ext/approx) package.
- SQLite 3.54.1, with an [upstream fix](https://sqlite.org/src/info/535a77cf5a).

## Database
- Extension metadata is now cached in memory to avoid redundant database updates. Thanks to Minecraft0122 for work on this.
- Fixed SQL syntax error related to database clean task cleaning plugin data

- **Android SQLite:** `ATTACH` and DDL statements work. Every statement in a multi-statement string runs, and its rows are counted. `replace()` is no longer confused with a `REPLACE` statement.
- **A `begin()` inside a transaction is a savepoint on every driver.** The JVM PostgreSQL and MySQL drivers used to send a second `BEGIN`, so a nested commit committed the outer transaction.
- **Cancellation:** a cancelled `acquire()` or `begin()` gives its connection or transaction back, on native, JVM SQLite and An

- Stoppable PostgreSQL LISTEN, with no leaked connections (also fixes `PgmqConsumer`).
- Migrations: large files, `?` operators, trigger bodies and MySQL dump comments all work.
✅ No database migrations required.
- JVM MySQL: unknown URL properties are rejected, and sessions use UTC.
- SQLite stores `LocalTime`/`LocalDateTime` with seconds always written.
- `batchInsert` / `batchUpdate` on MySQL and MariaDB.
- No more native process aborts on valid PostgreSQL/MySQL values or malformed URLs.
- No deadlocks
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/smyrgeorge/sqlx4k/compare/1.16.0...1.16.1

- Native MySQL: `_bin` collated text no longer hex-encoded; generated `insert()`/`update()` fixed (error 1064)
- **Exact decimals**: NUMERIC/decimal decoding on every driver, including binary NUMERIC and `NUMERIC[]` on native PostgreSQL (#184).
- Android SQLite: several connection-pool concurrency fixes
- **Generated ids**: `executeWithResult()` returns `rowsAffected` + `lastInsertId` (MySQL, SQLite, SQLCipher). Closes #182.
- Native PostgreSQL: binary NUMERIC decoding, no panic on undecodable columns (#184

This release adds row streaming with `fetch()` on every driver, a Gradle plugin that configures sqlx4k from a single `sqlx4k { }` block, and database-reported error details on `SQLError`.
- **Database error details on `SQLError`**: new `sqlState` (PostgreSQL, MySQL), `nativeCode` (MySQL, SQLite) and `kind` properties. `SQLError.Kind` classifies errors portably: `UniqueViolation`, `ForeignKeyViolation`, `NotNullViolation`, `CheckViolation`, `ExclusionViolation`, `Deadlock`, `SerializationFailure`, `LockTimeo

This release adds optimistic locking, transaction savepoints and MariaDB batch inserts, and hardens the native drivers so connection errors are reported instead of aborting the process.
- **MariaDB dialect**: `batchInsert` via multi-row `INSERT ... RETURNING` (MariaDB 10.5+). `batchUpdate` is reported as unsupported on MariaDB.
- **No more native panics**: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and SQLite-Cipher drivers return driver/connection errors (Io, Tls, Protocol, Decode, ...) as `SQLError` instead of panicking.
